title: LOUISVILLE VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Louisville Village Board met Thursday evening and moved swiftly through their agenda, once they got past public comments.

Sue Bailey and members of the group CATS or Clip And Tip Strays spoke to the board about their effort to reduce the stray and feral cat population in Clay County and specifically in Louisville.  Sue Bailey talked about her effort for decades of caring for cats in her neighborhood and spaying and neutering the cats when they could.  She supports the effort of the group to take up the effort of reducing the excess population of cats much as she did in year’s past.  She also took the time to reflect on how much these cats have meant to her and her late husband Speedy Bailey.  She became emotional about how they referred to the cats as their kids and after his passing, how they served to comfort her in his passing and continue to do so to this day.  Nicola Wattles went over the progress of their effort to practice the TNR method, or Trap, Neuter and Return.  She said they have spayed and neutered 120 cats and usually do 20 in a day when they host a clinic once a month but are considering doing two a month.  Wattles thanked the board again for their support and said their effort will see fewer stray and feral cats in the long term.

When the meeting moved on to regular business, trustees approved the meeting agenda and past meeting minutes and the bills.

Mayor Chris Rinehart asked the board to consider approving a renegotiated agreement with UGM or Utility Gas Management, the company that supplies natural gas to the village.  He said the intergovernmental agreement preserves the discount rate they pay but it also includes language that allows the mayor to act in certain circumstances without requiring action by the full board.  Trustees voted unanimously to approve the agreement.

The mayor stated that there is interest in the former clinic building at 935 Bryant Street and along Route 45.  The business would require a Liquor/Gaming License and he asked them to approve moving to process forward.  Trustee Chuck Smith commented that his office has the authority to approve the measure without the board.  Mayor Rinehart countered that he was aware of that, however he was not going to take action on that matter without the board’s input.  The measure passed 4-2 with Tim Davis and Mary Frazer voting no.

The Ameren Franchise Agreement approved in February was the next topic of discussion.  Mayor Rinehart provided trustees with a little more information about the agreement where the village is now paid rather than receiving electricity as it did in previous years.  Ameren stated that the village forfeited the free electricity it received when it entered into an aggregation agreement with another vendor in 2009.  Ameren no longer offers electric credits to municipalities.  It now simply pays for the access to customers.  In Louisville’s case, it will receive $8,000 per year in the new agreement approved last month.

Utilities Superintendent Troy Elwood led the board through the next agenda item of giving compensation to village employees for earning their Natural Gas License.  He said an employee was told they would earn a bonus when they attained the license.  Members voted to approve the bonus unanimously.  Other bonuses may be awarded when an employee achieves a license in other fields too

Trustees began a short discussion of the FY2027 tentative budget.  Mayor Rinehart said it’s not quite ready.  The board learned it needs to be finished by March 31 and laid open for 30 days of public inspection and then requires a public hearing before final adoption by April 30 and goes into effect at the start of the new fiscal year on May 1.

During open time, Mayor Rinehart informed the board about the passing of Mike Bridges of Charleston Engineering of Olney.  He reminded them and the public about the many projects that he has been involved in for the past several decades including the recently complete Louisville Pavilion.  His memorial service is this evening at Kistler-Patterson Funeral Home in Olney.  He closed by saying that he will be sorely missed.  With all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: SATURDAY EARLY VOTING
full_story:
The Clay County Clerks office will be open tomorrow from 8 to Noon for early voting.

Early voting for Illinois’ March 17th General Primary Election continues through Monday.  Registered voters may cast ballots at the county clerk’s office today and Monday from 8 am to 4 pm.

Voters requesting a vote-by-mail ballot should note that selecting a nonpartisan ballot may result in no ballot being issued if no nonpartisan questions appear on the ballot.

Illinois does not require voters to declare a party when registering.  Instead, voters choose which party ballot they want at the time they vote and may select a different party in future primaries.

title: FLORA STUDENTS EXCEL
full_story:
Flora High School students, Sydney Dawkins, Kristen Pipher, Payton Scroggins, Paul Hudson, Qynlin Brown, Hayden Young, Rylie Baker, and Meredith Woolever placed among the top students in Illinois in the 2025 Office Specialist (MOS) State Championship for Fall Semester.

The MOS State Championship consists of six certification exams covering Microsoft Office products such as Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.  Sydney Dawkins placed 2nd in Excel; Kristen Pipher placed 1st in PowerPoint, with a perfect score, and 4th in Excel; Meredith Woolever placed 2nd in PowerPoint, with a perfect score, and 6th place in Word; Paul Hudson placed 3rd in PowerPoint, with a perfect score, and 3rd in Word; Qynlin Brown placed 4th in PowerPoint and 2nd in Word; Payton Scroggins placed 1st in Word, with a perfect score; Hayden Young placed 7th in Word, and Rylie Baker placed 9th in Word.  1st place winners earn the opportunity to attend the Microsoft National Competition in Nashville, Tennessee in June.  Students attending the National competition compete against other students from 50 states for scholarships.  Kristen attended the competition last summer in Dallas.

These MOS exams are industry-standard assessments and to finish this high in the state proves to potential employers that you have mastered the skills.  Flora High School has been a Microsoft testing facility for six years.  In addition, Flora High School was one of three schools chosen for the Certiport Marketing Video for the state of Illinois to encourage students to earn these certifications.  The video can be found on youtube at “The Impact of Industry Certifications in Illinois”—full length.

Alicia Westjohn, Flora High School Business and Computer teacher earned an award for Outstanding Educator in Illinois during the MOS State Championship.  She also presented at the 2025 Dallas Conference where she shared “How to Develop a Thriving Certification Program in a Small Town”.  Many supportive local businesses in the Flora area were discussed as well as the successes of her many students at Flora High School.

title: GET OUT THE VOTE TOUR
full_story:

title: TRIPLETT PASSES
full_story:
Chris Triplett a well-known funeral director who owned and operated the McGriff & Triplett Funeral Homes in Louisville and Kinmundy has passed away.

He was a sixth-generation funeral director, raised in Staunton, Illinois, where he spent most of his life in his grandparents’ funeral home.  He graduated from St Louis College as the valedictorian of the 2003 mortuary science program and even served as a clinical embalming instructor.

He and his wife, Sandra, previously owned and operated McGriff & Triplett Funeral Homes before purchasing Wilson Funeral Home in Kahoka, Illinois, with plans to rename it Wilson & Triplett Funeral Home.  Chris and Sandra were dedicated to their community, actively involved in church activities, and enthusiastic about settling into their new home in Clark County.

Chris Triplett passed away unexpectedly, leaving behind a family struggling with the financial burden of funeral expenses due to his recent divorce and loss of businesses.  A GoFundMe page has been set up by his niece, Kayla Miller, to help honor his wishes for a full funeral service.

title: TATE DROPS CASE
full_story:
Convicted killer Ray E. Tate has dropped a bid to withdraw his guilty plea to multiple kidnapping and firearm charges in Clinton County.

In Clinton County Circuit Court Friday, Tate officially dropped a motion to withdraw his guilty plea and vacate his sentence.  The move came after the Clinton County State’s Attorney first asked Judge Douglas Gruenke to strike Tate’s motion.  The judge rejected the request and gave Tate the opportunity to argue his case.  Tate declined and abruptly withdrew his motion.

In addition to the life sentence in Wayne County, Tate is serving two 30-year sentences in Clinton County for aggravated kidnapping, a 30-year hitch for home invasion while firing a gun and another 10 years for aggravated possession of a stolen firearm.  The Clinton County sentences will be served concurrently.

While the Clinton County cases have been resolved, Tate still has an appeal pending in his Wayne County murder case.  After Judge Denton Aud denied Tate’s motion to withdraw his guilty plea and vacate his sentence, he appealed the ruling to the Fifth District Court of Appeals.  The appeal is still pending.

Meanwhile, Tate is serving his life sentence at the maximum security Menard State Penitentiary at Chester for the December, 2021 slaying of Wayne County Sheriff’s Deputy Sean Riley.

title: CARMI JAILER CHARGED
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) Division of Criminal Investigation Zone 8 Special Agents arrested 57-year-old Darren R. Hays of Carmi, for six counts of Custodial Sexual Misconduct, a Class 3 Felony, and one count of Official Misconduct, also a Class 3 Felony.

On November 11, of last year, the White County Sheriff’s Office requested ISP’s assistance with an investigation involving Hays, a correctional officer at the White County Jail.  An extensive investigation revealed that Hays allegedly engaged in a sexual relationship with a female inmate while on-duty at the jail.

On Wednesday, ISP Special Agents presented the case to the Gallatin County State’s Attorney’s Office, who filed the above-mentioned charges and issued an arrest warrant.  ISP arrested Hays the same day and transported him to the Saline County Detention Center where he remains in custody pending his first court appearance.

title: BOBCAT SEASON
full_story:
The 25-26 Illinois bobcat season concluded on February 15th with 627 bobcats harvested by hunters and trappers.

A total of 405 (62%) bobcats were taken by hunting, while trapping accounted for 222 (34%) of the harvest.  Twenty-seven (4%) were salvaged by permit holders from circumstances such as roadkill.  The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) issued 2,000 permits for the 2025 season out of 9,700 bobcat lottery applicants.

Hunters and trappers in Jefferson County reported 33 bobcats, which was the most for any county this year.  Macoupin County was second with 28 bobcats reported.

IDNR continues to monitor the status of bobcats and will evaluate the program as new data become available from ongoing research.

title: PATRICK’S DAY
full_story:
St. Patrick’s Day brings parades, parties and an important reminder from the Illinois Department of Transportation, Illinois State Police and more than 200 additional law enforcement agencies throughout the state: “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” and “Drive High. Get a DUI.”

“Driving after consuming alcohol, using cannabis or becoming impaired by any substance is dangerous and potentially deadly,” said Stephane B. Seck-Birhame, IDOT’s bureau chief of Safety Programs and Engineering.  “Prescription medications, drugs and combinations of substances can impair your judgment, attention and reaction time, so designate a driver before it’s too late to make a safe decision.”

According to IDOT data, on St. Patrick’s Day from 2020 through 2024, Illinois recorded 3,315 crashes statewide, including 671 injury crashes and 10 fatal crashes, resulting in 10 fatalities involving alcohol or cannabinoids.

This year’s St. Patrick’s Day enforcement and awareness effort begins today and extends into the early hours of March 23rd.

“Often celebrated with green beer and Irish whiskey, ISP is reminding you to celebrate smartly this St. Patrick’s Day by designating a driver, arranging a ride share or asking a friend to pick you up if you plan on drinking,” said ISP Division of Patrol Col. Chris Owen.

The St. Patrick’s Day “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” and “Drive High. Get a DUI” enforcement campaign is funded with federal traffic safety grants administered by IDOT.  These efforts are supported by ISP and local law enforcement agencies across the state.  The campaigns are reinforced by IDOT’s “It’s Not a Game” initiative spotlighting safe driving and highway safety throughout Illinois.
